sourceAnchors.reason: Constructor-confined HashMap never escapes: all key/version validation precedes copying, final keys stores Map.copyOf and local copies is not retained. Mutable key arrays are private and every encrypt/decrypt/close is guarded by private stateLock. ConcurrentHashMap would not add safety or enforce that lock. New factory is only stored, not invoked in the constructor, so the constructor-local map still never escapes and nullable factory is rejected before copying.
sourceAnchors.message: If you run in Java5 or newer and have concurrent access, you should use the ConcurrentHashMap implementation

sourceAnchors.reason: The null operand is the independent negative input to the Java record value contract, and false is the literal expected value. This is not a production null-check idiom and cannot be replaced by receiver==null without ceasing to test equals. No suppression or private reflection.
sourceAnchors.message: Avoid using equals() to compare against null
